q: Under Sec. 8.5 (Separate Consultants), if the Client hires a Consultant separately (apart from the Architect), how is that Consultant's fee handled?
o: It is paid by the Contractor as part of the construction budget
It is split 50/50 between the Client and the AoR
It is deducted from the Architect's RPF
It is on the account of, and paid directly by, the Client
n: "Should the Client hire separately the services of the Consultant, the fee of the Consultant shall be on the account and paid directly by the Client." Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 8.5

q: Under Sec. 8.1.2, what is the second manner by which full-time supervision services may be provided?
o: The Architect subcontracts the entire supervision role to the Contractor
The Architect works purely as Consulting Architect for full-time supervision services only, or as the CSG — without also acting as AoR
The AoR and CSG are merged into a single mandatory entity by law
The Owner personally supervises construction without any Architect involvement
n: 8.1.2 states the Architect may work "as Consulting Architect for fulltime supervision services only or as the CSG" — i.e., not in the dual AoR capacity of 8.1.1. Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 8.1.2

q: An Owner tells the Architect she wants a supervisor physically present at the site every working day throughout construction, rather than the occasional site visits typical of ordinary design-phase supervision. Under which service should this arrangement be contracted?
o: Pre-Design Services (SPP Doc. 201)
Full-Time Construction Supervision Services (SPP Doc. 204-A)
Post-Construction Services (SPP Doc. 205)
Regular Design Services' built-in Periodic Construction Supervision (SPP Doc. 202)
n: Daily, continuous on-site presence is precisely what "full-time" supervision under SPP Doc. 204-A provides, distinct from the periodic/part-time site visits already folded into Regular Design Services' Construction Phase fee. Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 8 (title); cf. SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.4.6

q: While an Architect is providing full-time supervision under a 204-A contract, the Owner decides to hire a specialized acoustics Consultant directly, bypassing the Architect. How should the fees be arranged, and what must the Architect still be paid for?
o: The Contractor pays both the Consultant and the Architect out of the construction budget
The Consultant's fee is paid directly by the Client/Owner, and the AoR is additionally paid 5% of that Consultant's fee for coordinating/relating the Consultant's work to his own
The Architect absorbs the Consultant's fee out of his own RPF
The Architect is no longer entitled to any coordination fee since he did not hire the Consultant
n: Per Sec. 8.5, the separately-hired Consultant is paid directly by the Client, while the AoR separately earns 5% of the Consultant's fee for the coordination work. Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 8.5

q: Which of the following is NOT one of the methods of compensation listed under Sec. 8.2 for Full-Time Construction Supervision Services?
o: Retainer as a standalone method
Mixed Methods of Compensation
Multiple of Direct Personnel Expense
Lump Sum or Fixed Fee
n: Sec. 8.2's six methods are: 8.2.1 % of PCC, 8.2.2 MDPE, 8.2.3 Professional Fee Plus Expenses, 8.2.4 Lump Sum or Fixed Fee, 8.2.5 Per Diem/Honorarium Plus Reimbursable Expenses, 8.2.6 Mixed Methods. A standalone "Retainer" method is not among them (it appears instead in the Specialized Architectural Services methods list, SPP Doc. 203). Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 8.2.1–8.2.6

q: Per Sec. 8.4 (Manner of Payment), how may the Architect bill and be paid during the construction period?
o: In progress payments proportional to the percentage of progress of completion of the construction work
Only through advance payment made before construction starts
Only as a single lump sum after the Certificate of Completion is issued
Strictly on a fixed monthly retainer regardless of progress
n: 8.4 states the Architect "may bill and be paid for the progress payments during construction proportional to the percentage of progress of completion of the construction work." Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 8.4

q: Under Sec. 8.1 (Manner of Providing Services), in how many distinct ways may the Architect enter into a contract with the Owner for full-time construction supervision services?
o: Three
Four
One
Two
n: Sec. 8.1 states there are two ways: (8.1.1) dual capacity as Architect-of-Record and Consulting Architect/CSG, or (8.1.2) as Consulting Architect for full-time supervision only/CSG. Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 8.1

q: What is the Recommended Professional Fee (RPF) under Sec. 8.3 for Full-Time Construction Supervision Services?
o: 1.5% to 3% of the PCC
10% to 15% of the Cost of Work
1% to 1.5% of the Project Construction Cost (PCC)
4% to 6% of gross rentals
n: Sec. 8.3 states the RPF "is 1% to 1.5% of the Project Construction Cost (PCC)." Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 8.3

q: A different project has a PCC of PHP 30,000,000.00, with the Architect engaged at the high end of the RPF (1.5%). Construction is suspended after reaching only 70% completion. What pro-rated RPF amount is the Architect entitled to under Sec. 8.4?
n: Total RPF = 1.5% × PHP 30,000,000.00 = PHP 450,000.00. Pro-rated at 70% completion = PHP 450,000.00 × 70% = PHP 315,000.00, payable to the Architect by the Client per Sec. 8.4. Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 8.3–8.4

q: Under Sec. 8.1.1, when the AoR himself undertakes full-time supervision in a dual capacity, how may the day-to-day site work be carried out, and against what reference document?
o: He may delegate the work only to the Project Manager's own staff
He may assign his staff to undertake the full-time supervisory work, performing the tasks enumerated in the Architect's Guidelines
He must personally perform all supervisory duties without delegating to staff
He must hire an unrelated third-party CSG to do the work instead
n: 8.1.1 states he "can assign his staff to undertake the fulltime supervisory work to perform the works as enumerated in the Architect's Guidelines." Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 8.1.1

q: For the same PHP 20,000,000.00 PCC project, what is the full recommended fee range the Architect may charge for full-time supervision?
Under Sec. 8.5, what fee is the Architect-of-Record (AoR) entitled to for coordinating and relating the work of a separately-hired Consultant to the Architect's own work?
o: A flat honorarium set by the Board
10% of the Consultant's fee
5% of the Consultant's fee
1% to 1.5% of the PCC, same as the RPF
n: "The fee of the Architect-of-Record (AoR) for coordinating and relating the work of the Consultant to the work of the Architect will be 5% of the Consultant's fee." Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 8.5

q: An Architect who designed a project and wants to retain full authority to interpret his own drawings and directly ensure the Contractor's conformity with them should, under Sec. 8.1.1, take on full-time supervision by...
o: Acting in a dual capacity as Architect-of-Record and Consulting Architect for full-time supervision (or CSG)
Delegating full-time supervision entirely to the Contractor's own site engineer
Declining any supervisory role and letting the Owner hire an unrelated CSG
Acting solely as Consulting Architect for full-time supervision, unconnected to the design (per 8.1.2)
n: Sec. 8.1.1 is precisely the dual-capacity arrangement that keeps interpretive authority over his own drawings in the same Architect who is doing full-time supervision. Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 8.1.1

q: How does Full-Time Construction Supervision Services (SPP Doc. 204-A) differ from the Periodic Construction Supervision (PCS) already included in Regular Design Services (SPP Doc. 202)?
o: PCS applies only to government projects while 204-A applies only to private projects
PCS is a full 10% of the professional fee, while 204-A is rendered free of charge
They are identical services with different names

PCS under Regular Design Services covers only occasional/part-time site visits (compensated as just 5% of the Professional Fee in the Construction Phase), while Full-Time Supervision under 204-A is a distinct, separately-contracted, continuous on-site service with its own 1%–1.5% of PCC fee
n: SPP Doc. 202's Construction Phase reserves just 5% of the Professional Fee for Periodic Construction Supervision (the other 5% is for the Architect's civil-code liability); continuous, full-time on-site supervision is instead a wholly separate, additional service under SPP Doc. 204-A, compensated at 1%–1.5% of PCC. Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 8.3; cf. SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.4.6

q: Where does "Full-Time Supervision Services (SPP Doc. 204-A)" fall within the Architect's overall range of services, and what immediately follows it?
o: It is a subsection of Post-Construction Services with no independent SPP document number
It is the first of ten major services, followed by Pre-Design Services
It is the last of the ten major services, with no further sections after it
It is the fourth of ten major services (after Pre-Design, Regular Design, and Specialized Architectural Services), immediately followed by Sec. 9, Construction Management Services (SPP Doc. 204-B)
n: The Architect's services are divided into ten major services, of which Full-Time Supervision (SPP Doc. 204-A) is the fourth (after Pre-Design 201, Regular Design 202, Specialized 203); Sec. 8 is immediately followed in the source by "Sec 9: CONSTRUCTION MANAGEMENT" (SPP Doc. 204-B). Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 8 (heading and transition to Sec. 9); cf. Rule III, Schedule of Fees

q: Sec. 8.2.1 identifies which cost basis for computing full-time supervision compensation on a percentage basis?
o: Percentage of Project Construction Cost (PCC)
Percentage of the Consultant's fee
Percentage of the Direct Personnel Expense
Percentage of Cost of Work
n: 8.2.1 is "Percentage of Project Construction Cost." Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 8.2.1

q: Under Sec. 8.4, if the construction work is not completed, who is responsible for paying the Architect the pro-rated RPF component?
o: The Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture
The Client (Owner)
No one — the Architect forfeits the balance
The Contractor
n: "Should the work be not completed, the pro-rated RPF component shall be paid to the Architect by the Client." Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 8.4

q: Under Sec. 8.1.1, what does it mean for the Architect to serve in a "dual capacity" for full-time supervision services?
o: He acts simultaneously as Architect-of-Record (AoR) and as Consulting Architect for full-time supervision (or CSG)
He works for both the Owner and the Contractor at the same time
He splits his fee equally between two consulting firms
He supervises two separate projects concurrently
n: 8.1.1 describes working "in a dual capacity as Architect-of-record and as Consulting Architect for fulltime supervision services or as the Construction Supervision Group (CSG)." Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 8.1.1

q: A project has a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of PHP 20,000,000.00. Using the low end of the Recommended Professional Fee (1%) for Full-Time Construction Supervision Services, what is the Architect's fee?

Construction on a project under a Full-Time Supervision contract is abruptly halted at 70% completion because the Owner runs out of funds. Under Sec. 8.4, what is the Architect entitled to, and from whom?
o: The full 100% RPF, paid by the Contractor
A penalty fee equal to double the RPF, paid by the Contractor
The pro-rated RPF component corresponding to the work's progress, paid by the Client
Nothing, since the project was never completed
n: Sec. 8.4 entitles the Architect to the pro-rated RPF for work actually done, payable by the Client, when construction is not completed. Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 8.4

q: In SPP Doc. 204-A, what does the abbreviation "CSG" stand for?
o: Construction Site Group
Construction Supervision Group
Consulting Services Group
Contractor Supervision Guild
n: CSG = Construction Supervision Group, referenced in both 8.1.1 and 8.1.2 as an alternative arrangement for providing full-time supervision. Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 8.1.1–8.1.2

q: A smaller project has a PCC of PHP 8,500,000.00. What is the Architect's fee at the high end of the RPF (1.5%)?
A Client separately hires a structural Consultant for PHP 300,000.00 in fees. What coordination fee is the AoR entitled to under Sec. 8.5?
Sec. 8.2 (Method of Compensation) states that compensation for Full-Time Construction Supervision Services may be based on...
o: One or more of six listed methods, including percentage of PCC, MDPE, professional fee plus expenses, lump sum, per diem/honorarium, and mixed methods
A fixed government-mandated per diem rate only
Percentage of Project Construction Cost only, with no other method allowed
Whatever rate the Contractor proposes
n: 8.2 lists six methods (8.2.1–8.2.6) and states compensation "may be based on one or more" of them. Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 8.2

q: Who actually performs the day-to-day full-time supervision work under SPP Doc. 204-A?
o: Only the Professional Regulatory Board itself
Only the Owner's own in-house maintenance staff
Exclusively the Contractor's foreman
Either the AoR's own assigned staff (dual-capacity arrangement) or a separate Construction Supervision Group/Consulting Architect
n: Per 8.1.1–8.1.2, the work is done either by staff the AoR assigns (dual capacity) or by a Consulting Architect/CSG engaged solely for full-time supervision. Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 8.1.1–8.1.2

q: What is the official SPP document title and number covering full-time construction supervision services?
o: SPP Doc. 203 — Specialized Architectural Services
SPP Doc. 204-A — Full-Time Supervision Services
SPP Doc. 202 — Regular Design Services
SPP Doc. 204-B — Construction Management Services
n: Sec. 8 is captioned "8: FULL-TIME SUPERVISION SERVICES (SPP Doc. 204-A)." Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 8 (title)

q: What does the compensation method in Sec. 8.2.2, "Multiple of Direct Personnel Expense," base the Architect's fee on?
o: Reimbursement of travel expenses only
A fixed lump sum regardless of personnel used
A multiplied rate applied to the Project Construction Cost
A multiplied rate applied to the direct personnel costs (salaries/labor) expended on the project
n: MDPE bases the fee on a multiplier applied to the direct cost of personnel/staff time assigned to the project. Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 8.2.2

q: A project's PCC is PHP 45,000,000.00 and the Architect is engaged at the low end of the RPF (1%) for full-time supervision. If construction has reached 40% progress of completion when a progress billing is made, how much should the Architect be paid at that point?
n: Total RPF = 1% × PHP 45,000,000.00 = PHP 450,000.00. Progress billing = PHP 450,000.00 × 40% = PHP 180,000.00, per Sec. 8.4's proportional-progress billing rule. Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 8.3–8.4

q: Per Sec. 8.1.1, why is the Architect-of-Record (AoR) considered to be in a good position to perform full-time supervision himself?
o: He does not need to coordinate with any separate consultants
He is legally required to remain on-site under RA 9266
He is in a better position to interpret his own drawings and documents and assure conformity by the Contractor
He is exempt from the Recommended Professional Fee schedule
n: As AoR, "the AoR is in a better position to interpret his drawings and documents and to assure conformity by the Contractor." Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 8.1.1

q: Using the same PHP 20,000,000.00 PCC, what is the Architect's fee at the high end of the RPF (1.5%)?
